name: Standard Scramble (from Foggy Lake)

pitch_detail.notes: 1-mile road walk from Barlow Pass, then the 3.3-mi Weden Creek Trail #724 climbs steadily through forest from ~2,300 ft to open basin terrain near 5,000 ft.
Boulder-hop past two lower tarns to Foggy Lake, often snow-covered into summer.
Boot path climbs boulder fields to a saddle on Gothic Peak's southeast ridge.
pitch_detail.pitch: Foggy Lake to SE ridge saddle

pitch_detail.notes: Traverse onto the north-side slate/talus slope to avoid the exposed Class 4 ridge-crest line; the final ~150 ft is the crux, with a possible summit moat late season.

descent_text: Reverse the ascent line — the correct SE-ridge descent is generally easier to pick out looking downhill than it was on the way up, and most parties who wandered onto the harder Class 4 rock on the ascent spot the easier Class 3 bypass ('sidewalk' ledge) on the way down. From the true summit, downclimb the short (~100 vertical foot) summit block via its broken south-side terrain rather than traversing climber's-left, which dead-ends above the exposed south face in sustained 4th-class ground. Continue down the scree/talus on the north side of the SE ridge crest (the climber's-right side on the way up) back to the Foggy Lake outlet on the same cairned line used on the ascent, then retrace the maintained Gothic Basin trail — through the basin meadows, the steep timbered switchback band, and the Weeden Creek ford — back to the Barlow Pass trailhead. This is a walk-off/downclimb descent with no rappelling required in normal summer conditions. The real hazards are loose rock and fall exposure on the summit block and upper scree, and, in early-season or wet/icy conditions, hard snow on the slabs and snowfield just below the ridge, where an ice axe (and caution on the creek crossing) is warranted. A short handline is occasionally carried by conservative parties for the final summit-block downclimb, but it is not standard gear for this route.
approach: Start at the Barlow Pass trailhead on the Mountain Loop Highway (19.3 miles east of the Verlot Public Service Center), on the Weeden Creek Trail / Gothic Basin trail (USFS #724). The first ~0.7 mile follows an old closed mining road before singletrack begins climbing steadily through forest; the trail fords Weeden Creek around the 1.1-mile mark (no bridge — the main reliable water source low on the route). From there the trail switchbacks up a steep, root-and-rock staircase, gaining close to 1,000 ft/mile through a roughly 2-mile crux band; this section holds lingering snow patches and old avalanche run-out debris across the tread well into early summer in heavy-snow years, and can require an ice axe. Around 3.5–4 miles the trail breaks out of timber into the open slabs and tarns of Gothic Basin (around 5,000 ft) — the last dependable water before the final push and a good bail-out point in poor weather. From the basin, continue up talus and slab benches roughly another 0.5–0.6 mile to the saddle above Foggy Lake (total to the lake is about 9.2 miles / 2,800–3,100 ft round trip per multiple trail sources), then drop slightly and traverse roughly 0.3–0.4 mile along/above the lake's shore to its outlet. At the outlet, leave the maintained tread for an intermittent, cairned climber's path onto Gothic Peak's SE ridge; stay in the scree climber's-right of the ridge crest rather than on the crest itself, following cairns past a small tarn at the base of a snowfield and up broken rock to the base of the summit block. Route-finding is the main approach-specific hazard: in early season, snow can bury the cairned line, and many parties inadvertently stray onto exposed Class 4 rock to climber's-left of the correct, easier line just below the summit block.
overview: Gothic Peak is the lower, more approachable of two summits (with Del Campo Peak, 0.5 mi northeast across Foggy Pass) reached from Foggy Lake in Gothic Basin. Despite a reputation as a simple talus walk-up, the standard route above the lake is a Class 3 scramble along the southeast ridge, finishing with a short (~150 ft), exposed class 3–4 summit block — treat it as a real scramble, not a stroll. The peak and basin are named for prospector William Gothic, one of the first to stake a mining claim there; the name was officially adopted in 1967. First recorded ascent was June 10, 1934 by Don Blair, Willard Carr, Norval Grigg, and Art Winder. Rock is a mix of sandstone, quartz diorite, and conglomerate-argillite and can be loose, especially in the summit gully.
beta: From the Weden Creek/Gothic Basin trail's end at Foggy Lake, skirt the lake (stay climber's left/south side) and pick up a boot path and cairns climbing boulder fields toward the saddle on Gothic's southeast ridge. From the saddle, most parties traverse onto the north-side slate/talus slope to bypass an exposed Class 4 line directly on the ridge crest, regaining the crest near the top for a final, exposed ~150 ft of Class 3 scrambling (with moves bordering Class 4) to the summit block. Route-finding above the lake is not obvious and is easy to lose on the talus.
gear: ice axe recommended if snow lingers in the gully/basin (common into July)
helmet strongly recommended — the summit gully sheds loose rock, especially with multiple parties on route
microspikes or light crampons useful on firm snow early season
bear canister required for overnight camping in Gothic Basin (no trees suitable for a bear hang)
fa: Don Blair, Willard Carr, Norval Grigg, and Art Winder, June 10, 1934 (first ascent of the peak)
